history.summary: NOTE - CSV DUPLICATE: this row (625, 'Kopeshwar Temple, Sangli') describes the SAME temple as CSV row 622 ('Kopeshwar Temple, Kolhapur'). The Kopeshwar Temple stands at Khidrapur village, Shirol taluka, Kolhapur district, Maharashtra, on the bank of the Krishna river — it is accessible from Sangli (~36 km) but is NOT in Sangli district. Merge this row with 622; keep only one record. The temple: an ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva as Kopeshwar ('the angry god'). Legend: after Sati's self-immolation at Daksha's yajna, the enraged Shiva punished Daksha by beheading him (Daksha was revived with a goat's head); Vishnu brought the furious Shiva to this spot to calm him, hence the name. Unusually, a shrine of Vishnu as Dhopeshwar stands as a linga alongside the Shivling inside the temple, and there is no Nandi directly before the sanctum — because Sati rode Nandi to her father's house. Celebrated as the 'Khajuraho of Maharashtra' for its erotic and mythological stone carvings, it is one of the finest examples of medieval Bhumija-style architecture, built on a star-shaped plan, with four parts: Swargamandapa (open circular hall of heavens without a roof, open to sun and moonlight), Sabhamandapa, Antarala-kaksha (vestibule) and Garbhagriha (sanctum), its base supported by elephant sculptures and its pillars carved with gods, goddesses and artists. The Shilahara rulers were Jain kings who nevertheless built and renovated Hindu temples. The Krishna takes a horseshoe (nalakar) turn at Khidrapur, giving the site its religious significance; the village was known as Koppan in ancient times.

town_description: Khidrapur (ancient Koppan) is a village in Shirol taluka, Kolhapur district, Maharashtra, on the bank of the Krishna river at the Kolhapur-Sangli border, about 60 km from Kolhapur and about 36 km from Sangli.

travel.road: Khidrapur is reachable by road from both Kolhapur and Sangli
